newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian 9-month titanium exports up nearly 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian 9-month titanium exports up nearly 40 pct.

text.p: Russian exports of titanium and of articles made of titanium over January-September rose 39.1 percent on year-ago levels to 16,890 tonnes, the State Customs Committee said on Friday.

In figures quoted by Interfax news agency, it said total September titanium exports were 2,265 tonnes, including 953 tonnes of unprocessed metal and powder, 471 tonnes of flat-rolled material and 653 tonnes of scrap.
The Netherlands was the main destination of deliveries, taking 639 tonnes, with Ireland taking 475 tonnes, Germany 441 tonnes, the United States 326 tonnes and Japan 175 tonnes.
September exports fell 8.9 percent on the previous month, but no absolute comparison figures were provided.
Russian imports of titanium ore in September were 2,400 tonnes, a third of August levels and Russia's lowest level yet this year.
About 82 percent, or 1,980 tonnes, of the imports came from Ukraine.
